hypothesis: Test whether expanded eligible outer-training reference galleries improve public B002 and adapted F003 scoring while preserving the original encoder-held-out query set. Every query excludes its whole content group from both known and unknown references. Reproduce completed S004c/d exactly before either expanded recipe; no fitting or feature extraction.
selection_policy: Exactly four preregistered recipes: public/adapted fixed-reference S004c/d controls, then public/adapted expanded-gallery comparisons. All coefficients and thresholds use only original calibration_query rows, never encoder-fit rows or outer labels. Both fold and pooled control predictions must pass before expanded recipes. No outer selection among the four recipes.
limitations: The 443/445 known calibration queries retain their original 1-2 true-class references after group exclusion; outer evaluation restores 2-3 references. This 50-100% true-class support increase is a calibration distribution shift, even though total inner/outer gallery counts differ by only 1-2 files.
Other held-out-query rows may serve as references. Calibration observations therefore share reference data and are statistically dependent; optimized inner scores are not an independent evaluation.
Only original held-out queries may calibrate an adapted encoder. The broader all-training-query crossfit used for frozen S002f is not used here, so this is not a matched S002f protocol comparison.
Adapted caches remain bound to their own audited outer-fold final checkpoint and file hashes; shared NPZ signatures alone do not establish encoder identity.
Repeated development-fold comparisons are not an unbiased final test or a hidden leaderboard score. Unknown identities and recording sessions are not fully labeled.
All 4529 original files and 447 labels remain in evaluation, including 89 zero-signal files with unknown fallback.
